name: Захист від зв’язки (1)
description:
In the previous lessons you have practised with pins. Pins force enemy pieces to stay where they are to prevent the loss of a more valuable piece hiding behind it.

Defending against a pin can be done by means of:

  • interposing a piece between the pinner and the pinned piece
  • capturing the pinning piece
  • creating a counterattack
  • adding defenders to the pinned piece

Study the examples to understand how it works.


What do you have to do?

Prevent material loss by a successful defense against a pin.

examples.text:
Black pins White queen.
White can solve this very easily by moving the pawn to c3.
White defends against the pin with interposing.

The black bishop attacks the white queen with a pin.
White breaks the pin by capturing the bishop with the knight.

examples.pgn: {[%csl Ye1,Rh8][%cal Rb4e1]} 1. Qh6+ {[%csl Yh8]} Kg8 2. Re3 1/2-1/2
examples.text:
The white queen is attacked and is pinned to the white rook behind her.
White defends with a counterattack.

The queen gives check on h6 (Qd2-h6+).
Black has to get out of check and has no time to take the rook.
White now moves the rook to a safe square.

examples.pgn: {[%csl Rd2][%cal Rb4e1]} 1. Qf4 {[%cal Rf4b8]} Rf8 2. Re3 1/2-1/2
examples.text:
In this position Black attacks the queen and the rook behind her.
White solves it with a counterattack.

He moves the queen to f4 (Qd2-f4) and attacks the black rook on b8.
This buys him time to save both the queen and the rook.

The white knight is pinned, and attacked by the black pawn.
White solves this by moving the knight.

The knight goes to d3 (Ne5-d3).
From there, it can defend the white rook on e1.
